name: Mahoran Langouste a la Vanille
description: Langouste à la vanille, seafood in a real vanilla-cream sauce, reflects Mayotte's shared Comorian culinary heritage and the wider region's status as a vanilla-growing area - shrimp stands in here for lobster as a more widely available substitute.
steps_detailed: Cook the garlic in a little butter or oil 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and cook 2-3 minutes until just turning pink.
Add the cream and vanilla, and simmer 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened.

name: Mahoran Mataba
description: Mataba, cassava leaves cooked in real coconut milk, a genuine Mahoran staple shared with Comoros - real cassava leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in.
steps_detailed: Cook the garlic in a little oil 30 seconds.
Add the spinach and coconut milk, and simmer 12-15 minutes until well combined.
steps: Cook the garlic in a little oil 30 seconds.

description: Riz au coco, rice cooked in real coconut milk, reflects both Mayotte's Comorian heritage and its French administrative ties.

name: Mahoran Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Mayotte's Indian Ocean coastal fishing tradition.

Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Mahoran Coconut Fish Curry
description: A coconut-based fish curry, reflecting Mayotte's shared Swahili and Comorian Indian Ocean culinary tradition.
steps_detailed: Simmer the coconut milk, curry powder, and tomatoes 5-6 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer 8-10 minutes until just cooked through.

name: Mahoran Pilao
description: Pilao, spiced rice cooked with meat, reflects genuine Swahili and Indian Ocean trade influence shared across Mayotte and the wider Comorian archipelago.
steps_detailed: Deeply brown the onion, 10-12 minutes, until golden.
Add the chicken, cumin, and cinnamon, and brown 6-7 minutes.
Add the rice and broth, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.

description: Beignets de banane, fried banana fritters, reflect Mayotte's French culinary influence merged with the island's abundant local fruit.
steps_detailed: Mix the mashed banana with the flour and sugar into a thick batter.
Fry spoonfuls, turning, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden.

name: Mahoran Samosas
description: Samosas, fried triangular pastries with a spiced filling, reflect genuine Indian Ocean culinary influence and are a beloved Mahoran snack.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion and curry powder, 6-7 minutes.
Cut the phyllo into strips, fill, and fold into triangles.
Fry, turning, 3-4 minutes, until deeply golden.

name: Mahoran Chapati
description: Chapati, a soft, layered flatbread, reflects genuine Indian Ocean culinary influence and is a beloved Mahoran bread.
steps_detailed: Work the flour with warm water and half the oil into a soft dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Roll thin, brush with the remaining oil, and coil before flattening to build real layers.
Cook in a hot, dry pan, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden.
